title: IntRange rejects upper bound when clamp=False
description: When using click.IntRange(min=1, max=10), passing the value 10 raises a BadParameter error because the upper bound comparison uses strictly less-than instead of less-than-or-equal.

files.tests/test_click_types.py:
import unittest
from src.click_types import IntRange, BadParameter


class TestIntRange(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lower_bound(self):
        r = IntRange(min_val=1, max_val=10)
        self.assertEqual(r.convert(1), 1)

    def test_upper_bound_inclusive(self):
        r = IntRange(min_val=1, max_val=10)
        self.assertEqual(r.convert(10), 10)

    def test_out_of_bounds(self):
        r = IntRange(min_val=1, max_val=10)
        with self.assertRaises(BadParameter):
            r.convert(11)
        with self.assertRaises(BadParameter):
            r.convert(0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

expected_baseline_error: BadParameter: 10 is not smaller than maximum 10
reference_patch:
--- src/click_types.py
+++ src/click_types.py
@@ -11,6 +11,6 @@
         if self.min_val is not None and value < self.min_val:
             raise BadParameter(f'{value} is smaller than minimum {self.min_val}')
         # Bug: strictly less-than rejects the upper bound itself
-        if self.max_val is not None and value >= self.max_val:
-            raise BadParameter(f'{value} is not smaller than maximum {self.max_val}')
+        if self.max_val is not None and value > self.max_val:
+            raise BadParameter(f'{value} is larger than maximum {self.max_val}')
         return value
reproduction_methodology: Instantiate IntRange(1, 10) and pass 10. Raises BadParameter unexpectedly.

+
+
 class Router:

         """Normalize URL path by ensuring leading slash and removing trailing slash."""
         if not path:
             return '/'
-        # Bug: strip('/') strips both leading and trailing slashes unconditionally

class TestEnvParseBool(unittest.TestCase):

        self.assertFalse(parse_bool('FALSE'))
        self.assertFalse(parse_bool('No'))
        self.assertTrue(parse_bool('TRUE'))
        self.assertTrue(parse_bool('Yes'))

     """Parse common boolean representations into a Python bool."""
-    # Bug: case-sensitive membership check
